Melting 273.15 K and normal boiling 373.15 K: the solvent model's constants (states::WATER_FREEZING_K, WATER_BOILING_K), which the apparatus must agree with. The primary values are 273.1525 K for melting at 101.325 kPa (W. Wagner, T. Riethmann, R. Feistel and A. H. Harvey, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 40 (2011) 043103, doi:10.1063/1.3657937) and 373.124 K for the normal boiling point on ITS-90 (W. Wagner and A. Pruss, J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 31 (2002) 387-535, doi:10.1063/1.1461829); the shipped constants differ from them by 0.003 K and 0.026 K, inside the apparatus's stated 0.5 K, and are kept so the two routes cannot disagree.

NOT A MEASURED TRANSITION AND NO LITERATURE VALUE IS CLAIMED: 473.15 K (200 degrees Celsius) is this bench's model threshold for driving the waters of crystallisation off in phase_route::hydrates, an editorial parameter of the dehydration route. Real dehydration is stepwise through intermediate hydrates and depends on heating rate and water vapour pressure; a primary thermogravimetric source has not been attached yet. Model threshold, kerotakis 2026-11-11 (no doi; not a literature citation).
